relationships.subject: Indomethacin
relationships.evidence_quote: With indomethacin administration, the gastric cells showed significant increases in cox-2 mRNA expression (Figure 1A).

relationships.subject: Walnut polyphenol extract
relationships.evidence_quote: However, in the presence of the walnut extracts, the expression of cox-2 mRNA was significantly decreased.

relationships.subject: Walnut polyphenol extract
relationships.evidence_quote: However, the WPEs significantly decreased the PGE2 levels.

relationships.subject: c-Jun
relationships.evidence_quote: When we knocked down c-Jun with siRNA, as shown in Figure 2G, in spite of the WPE administration, 15-PGDH was not increased.

relationships.subject: Nrf2
relationships.evidence_quote: The findings included that, when Nrf2 was knocked down, the walnut administration did not provoke HO-1 (Figure 4D)

relationships.subject: Walnut polyphenol extract
relationships.evidence_quote: significantly increased levels of RvE1 were noted in accordance with an increasing dose of the WPE even under the indomethacin challenge.

key_findings: Walnut polyphenol extract protected against indomethacin gastric damage via c-Jun/AP-1-driven 15-PGDH, Nrf2-dependent HO-1 and increased RvE1.
WPE reduced COX-2 and PGE2 while preserving 15-PGDH in vitro and in rats.
